ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's list of designated persons. Additionally, a risk-based approach is applied to identify Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) using commercial databases and enhanced due diligence for any PEP, family member, or close associate. The screening must be conducted at the time of incorporation, upon any change in ownership, and at least annually thereafter. All results must be documented and retained for a minimum of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Commercial Registry (Supreme Court Registration Office) - Online Name Search Portal (https://www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean (Hangul) and may include English transliteration. The name must consist of a distinctive element, a business purpose, and a legal form indicator (e.g., '유한회사' for LLC). The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name. For foreign entities, the name must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul, and the English version may be used as a secondary name. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a unique identifier, (2) a description of the business, (3) the legal form suffix, and (4) compliance with the prohibition of misleading terms.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 10589, as amended), especially Articles 167, 169-171, 288-292, 295, 317-318, 329-331, 383, 389, 393-394, together with the Presidential Decree on Commercial Registration and the Regulations on Registration of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court Registration Office, or the local District Court Registration Office having jurisdiction over the registered office of the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application (Certificate of Incorporation Registration) supported by the notarized Articles of Incorporation and the First Board of Directors Resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed under the Korean Commercial Act. The full subscribed capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be deposited into a domestic corporate bank account before the incorporation registration is filed. A Certificate of Balance issued by the bank must be submitted to the competent registry authority. For non-resident shareholders, inbound equity investment must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; no blocked escrow account is explicitly required by the Companies Act, but the deposit must remain unavailable until registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA

Company Name: Yuhan Hoesa (LLC)
Place: Seoul, Republic of Korea
Date: [Registration Date]

WHEREAS the Company is being formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea;

WHEREAS all incorporating shareholders have executed the Articles of Incorporation and their respective share subscriptions;

WHEREAS the Board of Directors is duly constituted and authorized to transact corporate business pursuant to Article 393 of the Commercial Act;

NOW, THEREFORE, the Board of Directors, acting with a lawful quorum, has resolved, and does hereby resolve, as follows:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the subscription of ordinary shares by the founding shareholders, as set forth in the share subscription documents, is hereby ratified, approved, and confirmed in all respects. The Board acknowledges that all subscribed shares have been issued, that the aggregate paid-in capital has been fully deposited into a bank account opened in the Company's name, and that the bank's certificate of balance shall be filed with the competent registry authority together with the incorporation application.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company's principal banking relationship shall be established with a legally licensed commercial bank in Seoul, and that the representative director, together with any other designated director, is hereby appointed as the authorized signatory with full power and authority to open corporate accounts, sign account mandate documents, execute banking forms, make deposits and withdrawals, and manage all corporate funds, subject to such internal approval limits as the Board may from time to time establish.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Company shall be established at [Registered Address], Seoul, Republic of Korea, and that the representative director is empowered to execute a lease, procure fixtures, and file the registered office notice with the District Court Registration Office. The Board specifically adopts this address for statutory, licensing, and tax purposes.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are appointed: [Name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] as Director of Manufacturing and Industrial Licensing; and [Name] as Statutory Auditor if required by applicable law. Each appointed officer has accepted such office and shall serve for the statutory term as specified in the Articles of Incorporation. The Representative Director is authorized to represent the Company before all courts, public registries, tax authorities, and administrative agencies, and to apply for all permits required for the Company's manufacturing operations.

5. IMPLEMENTATION. RESOLVED, that the Representative Director is authorized to prepare, notarize, execute, file, and prosecute all incorporation documents, tax registrations, environmental approvals, and industrial licenses, and to retain qualified Korean legal counsel and licensed tax accountants where necessary.

ADOPTED by the unanimous written consent of the Board of Directors on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and Related Constituent Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notary Public; Licensing Legal Counsel accredited in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporating shareholders must prepare the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name Yuhan Hoesa, the stated purpose covering design, manufacture, polishing, assembly, and wholesale of hard enamel lapel pins and related merchandising, the initial registered office address, the aggregate subscribed share capital, the number and appointment methods of directors, auditor provisions, and the method of public notice. The document must be signed and sealed by each incorporator. A licensed Korean notary must authenticate the identities of the incorporators and certify that the document complies with the Commercial Act and the notarial practice. For foreign shareholders, notarized passport copies, English/Korean translations, and any required apostille certifications must be presented. The final notarized copies will constitute the foundational instrument for capital payment and court registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Corporate Name Search Certificate from the Registry Information Network
Passport copies of all incorporators or corporate shareholders
Certificate of Foreign Shareholder Identity or Apostille
Power of Attorney in favor of local formation counsel
Memorandum of Share Subscription
Consent forms of proposed directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a deficiency notice, the incorporators shall amend the Articles of Incorporation, hold a re-execution meeting before the same notary, and re-authenticate all signatures. If any apostilled foreign document is rejected, the applicant shall obtain a corrective apostille through the competent Korean consular or issuing authority and re-submit before the end of the notarial appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Capital Deposit Account and Full Payment of Subscription Price
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank Licensed under the Banking Act; Foreign Exchange Bank and Trade Authority for inbound remittances
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director or the designated incorporator shall approach a licensed commercial bank in Seoul and open a temporary corporate account in the exact legal name of Yuhan Hoesa. The full subscription amount must be paid into that account by cash deposit or by electronic remittance before the incorporation registration is submitted. For non-resident shareholders, the foreign exchange bank shall verify the inbound transfer and issue a foreign investment report certificate in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Notification on Foreign Investment. The bank must not permit withdrawal of the deposited capital until the court registry confirms the successful incorporation. After the deposit clears, the applicant shall request a Certificate of Balance and Certificate of Deposit of Subscription Price, both to be delivered to local formation counsel for inclusion in the court filing package.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Identification documents of the account signatory
Corporate seal certificate if already available
Inbound remittance advice for foreign shareholders
Share Subscription Document
Bank mandated signatory form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account opening due to incomplete corporate documentation, the applicant shall complete the bank's customer due diligence form, provide beneficial ownership statements, and use the modeled constitution documents. If an inbound remittance is suspended by foreign exchange controls, the remitter shall re-route the funds with the correct code statement and investment type, or obtain a local bank authorization to credit the temporary account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening of the First Shareholders Meeting and Adoption of the Initial Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Shareholders Meeting; Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators shall convene a formal organizational meeting to record the appointment of the initial directors and auditor. Immediately thereafter, the appointed directors shall convene the First Board of Directors Meeting to approve the subscription of shares, fix the paid-in capital, select the representative director, adopt the registered office, authorize corporate bank accounts, and approve the manufacturing license application strategy. All resolutions must be recorded in written minutes in the English language for the legal record, signed by every attending director, and dated. If the registry or any third party requires additional authenticity, the minutes shall be notarized. The resolution text used at the meeting shall be the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution prepared in the incorporation dossier, and any amendments must be reflected in the final certified minutes.
required_dossiers: Notice of Organizational Meeting
Share Subscription Register
Written Foreign Representation Statements
Minutes of the First Shareholders Meeting
Pro-Forma First Board Resolution
Written Acceptance of Office by Each Director and Auditor
Company Seal Specimen
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry later rejects the corporate minutes as incomplete or contrary to law, the directors may adopt a supplemental clear resolution ratifying all prior actions and deposit the corrected minutes with the notary. If a director declines to sign, the Board shall reduce the board quorum only if the Articles permit, or else call an extraordinary general meeting to replace the director before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with the District Court Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court Registration Office or the Local District Court Registration Office for the registered office location
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director or licensed legal counsel must file the electronic or physical incorporation registration application with the competent District Court Registration Office. The filing must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the Certificate of Balance from the bank, the first board resolution, proof of written consent of statutory officers, the share subscription report, and the prescribed statutory registration form. The registry officer will conduct a name and form examination and verify that all subscribed capital has been deposited and that the statutory officers are legally competent. Upon successful examination, the court will enter Yuhan Hoesa into the Commercial Registry and issue a certified Certificate of Incorporation Registration, at which moment the company acquires juridical personality. The applicant must pay the court registration fee and certificate issuance fee at the counter.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank Certificate of Balance and Paid-in Capital Evidence
First Board Resolution and Organizational Meeting Minutes
Share Subscription Statement
Consent and Appointment Forms of Directors and Auditor
Power of Attorney for Registration Agent
Applicant Identification and Corporate Seal Card
Postal or electronic stamp fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration officer issues a supplementary correction order (bogyeongmyeong), the corporation shall amend the identified clauses, re-notarize the Articles, obtain an updated capital certificate if necessary, and resubmit before the statutory deadline. If the registration is challenged for defective share payment, the applicant must show the updated certificate of deposit or arrange a receivable set-off with the bank and re-apply after cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration and Business License Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office (National Tax Service) and Municipal Manufacturing Business Registration Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of incorporation registration, the representative director must apply to the relevant Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service for the issuance of a Business License (corporate tax identification and business registration certificate). The application must be accompanied by the certified Certificate of Incorporation Registration, the registered office lease agreement, the corporate seal certificate, the representative director's identification, and the initial corporate bank account details. The tax office will verify the registered address and business purpose, assign the corporate registration number, and issue the Business License. The company must then register for electronic tax invoice issuance and file a VAT establishment report if applicable. If the facility will engage in cross-border sales, the representative director must also register the company with the Korea Customs Service for exporter status using the business license and proof of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation Registration
Certificate of Corporate Seal
Lease Contract for Registered Office and Production Site
Representative Director's Identification
Corporate Bank Account Certificate
Business License Application Form
Articles of Incorporation and First Board Resolution
VAT Registration Form and Electronic Tax Invoice Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office refuses the business location because the facility is not physically erected, the applicant shall submit the site photos, floor plan, lease contract rider, and an on-site inspection request. If the business license is delayed due to a mismatch between the corporate purpose in the Articles and the applied industrial activity, the company must amend the Articles to include die-struck brass cloisonné polishing and novelty enamel badge manufacturing, then refile an amended registration with the registry before requesting a revised Business License.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment and Korea Environment Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (low-impact small manufacturing category) applicable to micro-scale enamel pin painting and polishing operations; if degreasing or electroplating wastewater is generated in excess of small-scale thresholds, a Prior Environmental Consultation (Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment) may be required before the factory establishment registration is approved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to public sewer or water bodies must meet the Water Environment Conservation Act effluent limits: COD not exceeding 40 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 40 mg/L, total nitrogen 60 mg/L, total phosphorus 4 mg/L, and pH within 5.8-8.6. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from painting, enameling, and solvent cleaning booths must comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act; regulated painting facilities must maintain VOC collection efficiency of at least 90% and an exhaust gas concentration ceiling of 60 ppm as carbon, with solvent storage and waste solvent handling reported to the local environmental agency. Hazardous waste, including metal polishing sludge and spent enamel solvent, must be classified as designated industrial waste, stored separately in leak-proof containers, manifest-recorded within one month, and transferred only to a licensed hazardous waste treatment operator under the Wastes Control Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The company must obtain a Fire Facility Installation and Maintenance Certificate and a civil defense fire safety inspection approval for the production and storage areas under the Fire Service Act. The workplace must undergo a structural load inspection for the production line and warehouse mezzanines, pass an electric installation safety inspection, and submit an occupational safety risk assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. All workers in polishing, enamel filling, and brass etching areas must receive hazard communication training and be supplied with appropriate personal protective equipment, including chemical-resistant gloves and VOC respirators.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) in South Korea, the following procedure applies to obtain the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number (Business Registration Number, 사업자등록번호): 1) Obtain a Foreign Investment Notification (if applicable) from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) or KOTRA, and secure a Certificate of Foreign Investment (외국인투자신고필증). 2) Prepare the required documents: certified copy of the articles of incorporation, foreign investor's passport or corporate registration certificate (apostilled/legalized), lease agreement for the registered office, and a power of attorney appointing a tax representative (if the entity has no permanent establishment in Korea). 3) Submit the Business Registration Application (사업자등록신청서) to the local district tax office (세무서) having jurisdiction over the registered address, either in person or via the HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr) using the foreign investor's digital certificate (공동인증서). 4) The tax office reviews the application and issues the Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증) within 3-5 business days, which contains the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) that serves as both the corporate TIN and the VAT registration number. 5) The entity must also register for electronic tax invoice issuance (전자세금계산서) through HomeTax and obtain a digital certificate for e-invoicing. 6) If the entity has no permanent establishment, it must appoint a tax representative (납세관리인) to handle all tax filings and communications with the NTS.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the sovereign regulator under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a highly liberalized current account regime with full convertibility for trade in goods and services, interest, dividends, and ordinary remittances. Capital account transactions are conditionally liberalized and require statutory reporting or prior approval depending on the transaction size and nature. For a non-resident-owned limited liability company engaged in the manufacture and export of hard enamel lapel pins, capital importation via a foreign direct investment (FDI) qualifies as a capital account transaction under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The subscription of shares and receipt of the initial capital contribution must be reported ex ante to the MOEF or delegated institution (e.g., a domestic commercial bank) through a foreign exchange purchase and sale, and the proceeds can be credited to a dedicated Capital Escrow Account. Current account operations, including the receipt of export proceeds, are freely convertible but subject to documentary verification and the mandatory repurchase declaration of the export invoice. Profit remittance in the form of dividends is treated as a current account transaction; it is freely transferable after corporate tax withholding is settled and a tax clearance certificate or a tax receipt is presented to the remitting bank. The principal practical hurdle for a foreign shareholder is the need to demonstrate the lawful origin of the initial funds and to satisfy the bank's KYC/UBO diligence before the capital injection; after that, the KRW proceeds can be converted into USD or other hard currencies at the prevailing market rate without central bank quotas. No surrender requirement applies to export proceeds after the statutory collection period, but the exporter must repatriate the proceeds to Korea within the stipulated due date (normally 180 days from the export declaration, extendable upon bank approval) and may retain them in a foreign exchange account or convert them to KRW at will. The capital account remains constrained by the requirement to file a Foreign Exchange Transaction Report for every transaction exceeding USD 5,000 equivalent, and certain derivative transactions are limited to firms with underlying trade exposure. Overall, the regime is best characterized as convertible with prudential oversight, not a restrictive surrender-based system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 18 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Enforcement Decree, export receipts must be collected within the payment due date stated in the export contract, with a statutory default ceiling of 180 days after the export declaration date (extendable by the Minister of Economy and Finance in exceptional circumstances). The exporter must present the export declaration, commercial invoice, bill of lading, and bank receipt to the domestic bank through which the proceeds are received. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; exporters may retain the foreign currency in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or use the proceeds directly to settle import payables. However, the exporter is required to obtain a foreign exchange purchase and sale confirmation from the receiving bank and to file an export proceeds collection report within 15 business days of the collection date. Failure to comply triggers administrative penalties and the freezing of the Foreign Exchange Account until the matter is cured.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not legally viable as primary banking channels for a Korean resident entity. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act mandates that any entity providing payment services, foreign exchange brokerage, or deposit-taking facilities for Korean corporate clients must hold a license from the Financial Services Commission (FSC) and must be registered as a foreign exchange business operator with the Korea Customs Service or the MOEF. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex do not hold such licenses in Korea and cannot open local KRW clearing accounts on behalf of the entity without partnering with a licensed Korean bank. They may be used peripherally as a supplementary collection aggregator for inbound retail payments from platforms like Etsy or Stripe, but only through a licensed domestic bank as the underlying custodian of the settlement account. For real-time trade payments, tax remittances, and FX hedging, the entity must operate through a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank. The KYC standards of domestic banks are aligned to the FATF recommendations and typically require a larger documentation bundle than offshore EMIs; however, the legal and reputational risk of relying on an unlicensed EMI is deemed unacceptable for a treasury mandate. Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury, Medium as a sub-processor for e-commerce micro-collections where the EMI has a Korean banking partner and the funds are immediately settled to the domestic bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an initial corporate onboarding with a Korean Tier-1 bank, the statutory director(s) of the foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa must physically appear in a domestic branch for a face-to-face interview unless the bank accepts a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney authorizing a local resident or legal representative to attend on their behalf. Most major banks (KB, Shinhan, Woori, Hana) permit remote interview via videoconference only after the original corporate documents have been apostilled, translated by a certified Korean translator, and verified by the Korean consulate or the local notary public. The bank's compliance committee will require the physical presence of the beneficial owner or the authorized signatory for a formal interview regarding the nature of the business, the source of wealth, and the expected transaction profile. Remote opening without any physical or proxy presence is categorically not permitted under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. Therefore, the treasurer must plan for either a direct director visit to Seoul/Busan or a notarized POA with a Mongolian apostille and a certified translation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity where the foreign parent is a private company or a trust that does not have clear noxious web visibility
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full corporate registry extract (apostilled) from the home jurisdiction, a notarized UBO declaration listing every individual owning 25% or more, an organizational structure chart showing the chain from the ultimate controller to the Korean entity, passports and proof of residence of all UBOs, and a signed undertaking to notify the bank of any UBO change within 14 days. For foreign entities, provide a bank reference letter from a prime international bank confirming the UBO's identity and transaction activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection with funds originating from a high-risk jurisdiction or a cryptocurrency-adjacent source, which may trigger money laundering suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A source-of-funds memorandum with audited financial statements of the parent, personal bank statements of the UBO for the last 12 months, the loan agreement or equity subscription agreement, a certified copy of the foreign exchange transaction report to the MOEF, and a declaration that no funds derive from digital asset speculation. If the capital originates from a jurisdiction on the FATF or Korean Financial Security Agency grey list, provide a full bank-to-bank remittance chain, the commercial rationale for the injection, and a formal legal opinion from the jurisdiction's counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Screening alerts from sanctions/PEP databases, especially if the entity name does not appear in public databases or if the shareholder shares a name with a politically exposed person
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For each EPC (sanctions, PEP, and adverse media) hit, provide an official biometric page of the passport, a notarized explanation of the name variation, a certificate of good standing from the home registrar, and a detailed affidavit from the individual confirming no relation to sanctioned entities. In addition, the Korean bank will require a negative news search report from a reputable third-party screening provider (e.g., World-Check) for the UBO and all directors, and a written undertaking to immediately evident any material changes in the PEP status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared low-risk enamel pin manufacturing activity and the projected transaction volumes or counterparty geography, which may signal straw-man structuring
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a 3-year business plan with production capacity and order forecasts, the purchase orders from Etsy/Stripe or wholesale distributors, the underlying export contracts with foreign customers, logistics contracts, and insurance certificates. Also provide the commercial invoice templates and the technology/process description for the enamel pin manufacturing line. The bank will assess the consistency of the transaction graph; therefore, the dossier must include a trial balance of the original goods movement and expected cash flows. For any high-risk customer jurisdictions (e.g., sanctioned-risk freight forwarders), submit the end-user certificate and the export license where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The inbound FDI capital injection must be routed via the designated Capital Escrow Account opened at a Tier-1 domestic bank. The wiring instructions are a SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the parent's offshore bank to the Korean bank's corresponding USD or KRW account, with the intended beneficiary name registered under the Foreign Investment Report. The foreign exchange purpose code must be entered as 'FDI-190' for the acquisition of equity shares (Direct Investment) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Immediately upon receipt of the funds, the bank will issue a Certificate of Alien Investment Verification after the shareholder completes the Foreign Investment Registration with the MOEF or the bank itself if delegated. The verification process requires the submission of the Capital Subscription Agreement, the board resolution of the Korean company, and the passport of the subscribing shareholder. For compliance with the Bank of Korea's real name verification, the remitter must be an identical party to the shareholder, and the remittance message must contain the reference 'KR_YUHANGHOESA-SHARE SUBSCRIPTION-DIRECT INVESTMENT' to avoid misclassification. Once verified, the capital is transferred to the Basic Operational Currency Account with a transfer memo referencing the original verification number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For export-oriented sales of enamel pins, outbound and inbound trade settlements should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers and through documentary letters of credit (L/C) or documentary collections for conventional trade. For MT103 payments, the Korean bank will use the standard T/T (telegraphic transfer) field 70 with the export invoice number and the KOTRA/export declaration number. For commercial L/Cs, the beneficiary should open a sight L/C with a maturing period of 30-90 days through the Korean bank's trade desk; all documents (commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin) must be compliant. Documentary collections (incoterms D/P or D/A) are acceptable but carry higher non-payment risk; therefore, the treasury should use them only with established counterparties. The Korean bank will process export collections and import settlements under the same trade account, automatically netting off the proceeds against the export bill in the Foreign Currency Account. To mitigate FX revaluation risk, the treasury should maintain a natural USD portion of the account and only convert to KRW when local expenses (wages, utilities, VAT) arise. The bank's electronic trade settlement channel (e.g., Shinhan ETS or Woori Trade System) must be implemented to facilitate electronic document upload and real-time tracking.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Korean won (KRW) spot transactions for current and capital account settlement are freely permissible up to USD 5,000 per day without a reporting burden, but larger transactions require a Foreign Exchange Transaction Report.

Import/export forward contracts (non-deliverable or deliverable) with a maturity of up to 12 months are allowed for underlying trade exposure, provided the bank verifies the underlying export order or import contract; the nominal amount cannot exceed 200% of the actual export settlement amount in a rolling 12-month window.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/KRW are permitted for offshore entities into the domestic swap market as of the Market Stabilisation Mechanism authorized by the Bank of Korea and the MOEF; for the Korean resident entity, onshore forward deliverable contracts are preferred, but NDFs can be used as a hedge when the counterparty is an overseas financial institution and the settlement is made in USD against the BOK's announcement rate.

Currency swaps (FX swaps) with a notional of up to the capital injection amount are permissible to swap USD capital into KRW for working capital, with the swap counterparty restricted to domestic banks or the Seoul branch of a global bank; the swap must be entered into solely for hedging, not speculative purposes.

In addition, a KRW/USD barrier option overlay can be structured through a licensed Korean bank, but the entity must demonstrate a concurrent underlying trade receivable or payable. Derivative positions must be marked-to-market weekly, and the bank will require margin collateral of 5-10% for OTC derivatives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return with attached financial statements and tax reconciliation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts an additional tax of 20% of the tax amount not paid or reported; fraudulent understatement attracts an additional tax of 40% of the understated amount; overdue amounts carry a daily delinquency surcharge of 0.022% per day until paid. Persistent non-filing may trigger asset seizure, bank account attachment, and criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act. Korea does not apply an administrative strike-off to Yuhan Hoesa LLCs solely for tax delinquency; dissolution would require a court order or voluntary liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local municipal tax authority of the jurisdiction where the registered head office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity, no later than April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Understatement or non-filing triggers local tax additional charges of 20% of the understated or unpaid amount, increasing to 40% for fraudulent non-declaration, plus daily delinquency interest of 0.022% per day. Continued non-compliance may lead to compulsory collection and garnishment, but does not itself produce an administrative strike-off of the LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provisional Value-Added Tax Return for the first tax half
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By July 25 of the same calendar year for the first tax half comprising January 1 to June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or understatement exposes the company to VAT penalty additional tax equal to 10% of the unpaid or understated output VAT, or 20% for fraudulent non-reporting, plus a daily delinquency surcharge of 0.022% per day on overdue amounts. Repeat defaults may lead to compulsory collection, criminal referral, and cancellation of the business registration certificate, but no administrative strike-off of the corporate entity occurs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final Value-Added Tax Return for the second tax half
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 25 of the following calendar year for the second tax half comprising July 1 to December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or understatement attracts VAT penalty additional tax of 10% of the unpaid or understated output VAT, or 20% for fraudulent non-reporting, plus daily delinquency interest of 0.022% per day. Persistent non-filing may cause forced collection, criminal referral, and business registration cancellation, but does not create an automatic administrative strike-off for the LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements approval and external audit report lodgement when the statutory audit threshold is crossed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Yuhan Hoesa and the National Tax Service as part of the corporate income tax return filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be approved by shareholders within 6 months after fiscal year-end; the external audit report, when legally required, must accompany the corporate income tax return filed by March 31 of the following year for a calendar-year entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If a compulsory audit is omitted, the company may be subject to court-ordered coercion fines up to KRW 5 million, rejection of the unaudited financial statements by the tax authority, and regulatory sanctions under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; such omission does not in itself cause administrative strike-off, but may contribute to judicial dissolution proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean external audit regime and its Enforcement Decree, a Yuhan Hoesa LLC must appoint an independent certified CPA auditor and obtain a statutory audit if, at the end of the fiscal year, it meets any one of the following quantitative triggers: total assets are at least KRW 12 billion, total annual revenue is at least KRW 10 billion, or monthly average headcount is at least 100 employees; in addition, certain regulated industries, listed entities, and financial institutions are always subject to compulsory independent audit regardless of size. A company below all thresholds is not required to undergo a statutory external audit, but must still prepare and retain financial statements for corporate and tax purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (KIFRS) for listed and qualifying entities; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for non-public entities and SMEs are acceptable for a private Yuhan Hoesa; any statutory audit must be performed under Korean Standards on Auditing as issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a separate public annual UBO confirmation return for a private Yuhan Hoesa. Beneficial ownership information must be supplied when the company opens bank accounts or engages regulated financial institutions, and must be updated on a 30-day change basis for financial crime compliance under the Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information Act. For corporate registration purposes, any transfer of membership interests, change of directors, capital alteration, or registered office change must be filed with the local court registry within 2 weeks of the triggering event, and the transfer takes effect against the company only after entry in the Register of Members. There is no annual statutory UBO renewal form in the commercial registry system.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 1,800 per year for a Korean registered office address or corporate agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 30,000 for a full statutory audit under KIFRS or Korean GAAP when the threshold is crossed; USD 0 when the LLC remains below the statutory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (marginal rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 30 billion; progressive rates: 10% for income up to KRW 200 million; 20% for KRW 200 million-20 billion; 22% for KRW 20-300 billion; 25% over KRW 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific preferential free-zone or patent box applies to enamel pin manufacturing, but general incentives include: (i) R&D tax credit of 25-50% of qualifying R&D expenditure under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; (ii) investment tax credit of up to 3-7% for machinery used in manufacturing; (iii) employment tax credit for increased headcount; (iv) SME tax exemptions under the Tax Incentive Limitation Act; (v) potential foreign invested enterprise income tax holiday (100% exemption for 5 years and 50% reduction for 2 years) if the factory is located in a foreign-investment zone and meets high-tech criteria; (vi) additional deductions for overseas market development expenses incurred to export pins to Etsy and other channels.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) and associated schedules, filed electronically via HomeTax (홈택스; http://www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for a 31 December year-end, due 31 March of the following year) under Corporate Tax Act Article 60. A one-month extension may be applied for; non-resident filers subject to statutory audit may receive an additional two-month extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate worldwide sales revenue from the manufacture and sale of die-struck brass cloisonné and hard enamel lapel pins, including Etsy Direct Pay and Stripe settlement amounts, net of returns, allowances, and VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue attributable to the Korean entity. If the Korean LLC operates as a permanent establishment (PE) of a non-resident principal, only Korean-source revenue is taxable. Allocate revenue on the separate-enterprise principle and prepare a revenue trace schedule by customer jurisdiction and payment rail.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct manufacturing costs: raw materials (brass strips, cloisonné wire, high-temperature enamel paints, plating chemicals), direct labour for die-striking, enamelling, polishing, electroplating, inspection and packaging, and production overhead (depreciation, utility, repairs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For purchases from foreign related parties of raw materials or semi-finished blanks, confirm that the transfer price is arm's length and that the corresponding TP documentation is contemporaneous. Adjust inventory valuation to Korean GAAP / IFRS; if the entity uses free-zone inventory, segregation of local vs. foreign inventory is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: marketing and Etsy listing fees, Stripe transaction fees, payment gateway charges, shipping and logistics, customs brokerage, office rent, administrative salaries, insurance, information technology, and legal/accounting fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any home-office cost allocation from a foreign parent must be supported by a written allocation agreement and Korean statutory cost-deduction requirements. Only expenses incurred for the Korean PE are deductible; allocations must be arm's length and substantiated by time sheets or cost drivers. A TP adjustment may disallow unsubstantiated management fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit (Box 1 - Box 2) minus SG&A (Box 3). This is the ordinary operating profit on the pin business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity is the tested party under TNMM, the operating margin must fall within the interquartile range of comparable Korean or regional manufacturers. The NTS may reassess the arm's length margin and make a transfer pricing adjustment if the operating income falls outside the comparable range.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-core items: interest income, dividend income from third parties, foreign exchange gains/losses, gains/losses on disposal of fixed assets, donations, and other sundry non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest expense on debt from non-resident controlling shareholders is subject to the Korean thin capitalization rule (debt-equity ratio 3:1; 6:1 for financial institutions). The exceeding portion of interest is disallowed as an expense. Foreign interest or royalty income withheld at source should be credited here or in the foreign tax credit schedule of Box 8.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of operating income (Box 4) and non-operating income/expenses (Box 5).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation filing a domestic corporate return (surtax on a PE), correctly distinguish income attributable to the PE from other Korean-source income. If the entity is eligible for final settlement (withholding) on certain investment income, that income should be excluded from Box 6 and reported separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustment from pre-tax income to taxable income: add back non-deductible items (entertainment expenses above statutory limits, fines, penalties, cash gifts in excess of rules, illegal bribes), subtract tax-free income (e.g., certain dividend income), and subtract NOL carryforwards up to the 5-year limitation (or longer where applicable due to COVID-19 legislative measures).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply all statutory transfer pricing corrections (arm's length, thin capitalization, CFE rules). Loss carryforward is available only after submitting the loss carryforward schedule and is disallowed if the corporate identity is abused (e.g., shell company merger). For non-resident PE, loss recapture rules may apply upon the sale of the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Tax Computed, Credits, and Net Tax Payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the tentative income tax using the progressive corporate income tax schedule (10/20/22/25%), deduct the R&D tax credit, employment credit, facility investment credit, and tax relief for foreign income taxes. Then calculate the 10% local income tax surcharge on the assessed corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers claiming treaty-reduced withholding on dividends, interest, or royalties must attach the TRC and a beneficial ownership declaration. If the Korean entity is a domestic subsidiary of a foreign parent, dividend WHT is not a corporate tax item here but is handled at the time of distribution. Where foreign tax credits are claimed for withholding taxes on outbound income, attach Form 111 and the relevant evidence of tax paid abroad.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Corporate Tax Act: (i) failure to file a return on time attracts a negligence penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax where filed within 1 month of the deadline, rising to 30% after 1 month; (ii) understatement or overstatement penalties of 10% (if intentional) or 20% (if grossly negligent) apply on the difference between the reported and correct tax; (iii) daily overdue interest (currently 0.022% per day) accrues from the original due date until full payment; (iv) failure to attach statutory documents (TP master/local file, transfer pricing report) may trigger a formal documents non-compliance penalty; (v) persistent non-filing or fraudulent filing constitutes tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying criminal imprisonment of up to 2 years or a fine of up to 2 times the evaded tax and, in severe cases (tax evaded over KRW 500 million), imprisonment of up to 5 years; (vi) the NTS has authority to blacklist the company and its directors on the tax delinquents list, impose travel bans, and publicize the fraud.
